name: Planning Poker
highLevelGoals: The moderator aims to easily set up new Planning Poker games, manage the items to be estimated, and invite participants to ensure a smooth estimation session.
The moderator seeks to add, edit, and delete items for estimation dynamically, allowing for adaptability during the sprint planning process.
The moderator wants tools to select items for estimation, display estimates, and accept agreed-upon values efficiently to keep the planning session moving forward.
The moderator desires the ability to browse previous games, view transcripts, and export game data for record-keeping, analysis, or integration with other tools.
The moderator expects to create, log in, modify, and delete their account, with options for password recovery, to maintain control over their personal data and game history.
The moderator aims to configure game parameters such as estimation scales and participant limits to best suit their team's preferences and planning methodologies.
The estimator wants to easily join games, view the items being estimated, and understand the context of the current and past estimations to provide accurate input.
The estimator seeks the ability to submit and change their estimates flexibly, while also seeing other participants' estimates and notifications, to foster open discussion and consensus.
The participant desires tools like a countdown timer to manage discussion time and ensure focused conversations during the estimation process.
The participant aims for features like displaying thumbnail photos and consistent card order to make the game more personal and easier to follow.

The developer aims to build a site compliant with XHTML and CSS standards, functioning correctly across major browsers (IE 6/7, Firefox 1.5/2, Safari 2), and adhering to W3C accessibility guidelines to maximize user reach.
The developer aims to create database indexes to ensure that queries run as fast as possible, improving overall application responsiveness.
The user wants the application to respond quickly to their actions, ensuring a smooth and engaging experience without delays.
The user wants to be able to use Unicode, allowing them to input and display text in any language they prefer.
The user wants to see sensible and predictable URLs, contributing to a logical and transparent application experience.
The user wants to encounter helpful and informative error pages when issues occur, fostering trust in the system and its developers.
The researcher aims to access game results stored in a non-identifiable manner to conduct studies on estimation patterns and team dynamics without compromising user privacy.
lowLevelGoals: The moderator can initiate a new Planning Poker game session.
The moderator can send invitations to participants to join an active game.
The moderator can view a comprehensive list of all items currently added to the game for estimation.
The moderator can import a list of stories into the game from a spreadsheet file.
The moderator can copy and paste a list of stories directly from a spreadsheet into the game.
The moderator can permanently delete an entire Planning Poker game session.
The moderator can add a new item (e.g., user story) to the current game for estimation.
The moderator can modify the details of an existing item within the game.
The moderator can remove an item from the current game.
The moderator can designate a specific item to be estimated by participants.
The moderator can reveal all submitted estimates for the current item to the participants.
The moderator can finalize and record the agreed-upon estimate for an item.
The moderator can have the estimate field automatically populated with a calculated value (e.g., average) after estimates are revealed.
The moderator can manually enter an agreed-upon estimate for an item, overriding any calculated values.
The moderator can select a previously estimated story and initiate a new estimation round for it.
The moderator can view a list of all past Planning Poker games they have moderated.
The moderator can access a detailed transcript of a specific past game, including estimates and discussions.
The moderator can download the data from a past game in a specified format (e.g., CSV, JSON).
The moderator can download the transcript of a past game in HTML format.
The moderator can register a new user account with the system.
The moderator can authenticate and log into their existing user account.
The moderator can update their personal information or account settings.
The moderator can permanently remove their user account and associated data.
The moderator can initiate a process to reset their forgotten password.
The moderator can select or customize the set of estimation values (e.g., Fibonacci sequence) for a game.
The moderator can define the maximum number of participants allowed in a game.
The moderator can view the local timezone setting within the application.
The estimator can enter an active Planning Poker game using an invitation or game ID.
The estimator can see the details of the item currently being estimated.
The estimator can view a list of all items that have been added to the game for estimation.
The estimator can review the estimates and outcomes of previously estimated items within the current game.
The estimator can view their own prior estimates for the current story being estimated, if any.
The estimator can view other participants' prior estimates for the current story being estimated to facilitate discussion.
The estimator can scroll through a history of previous estimates for items in the current game.
The estimator can select and submit an estimation value for the current item.
The estimator can modify their previously submitted estimate before the moderator reveals all estimates.
The estimator can see which participants have submitted an estimate for the current item before the estimates are revealed.
The estimator receives a real-time notification when another participant submits an estimate.
The participant can initiate a countdown timer for discussion periods.
The participant can manually reset the countdown timer to its initial duration.
The system automatically resets the countdown timer after an estimate is accepted or a new item is selected.
The participant's profile picture or avatar is shown next to their name.
The system ensures that estimation cards are displayed in a fixed, predictable order for all participants.
The researcher can retrieve game results where all personally identifiable information has been removed or anonymized.
